title: What If 1 Nuke Hit a US Carrier Group at Sea?
description:
What would one nuclear bomb do to a US aircraft carrier group at sea? This is a minute-by-minute simulation of one 10-kiloton burst beside a carrier strike group, ring by ring, built from the Navy's own nuclear tests at sea and published blast models.

Ten past one in the morning, open Pacific: a nuclear weapon bursts beside a US carrier strike group. Twenty minutes earlier, a submarine fired one missile. The question is what one small bomb does to a ship of about 100,000 tons, and how far the damage reaches.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. It is not a forecast, names no real ship or country and uses no real date. The Wigwam and Crossroads tests, the B-59 submarine incident and the 1991 withdrawal of naval tactical nuclear weapons are real; scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen, facts REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY.

- FAS, Nuclear weapons at sea (Kristensen, 2016): https://fas.org/blogs/security/2016/02/nuclear-weapons-at-sea/
- CRS, Navy nuclear weapons and SLCM-N (2026): https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-01-08_IF12084_03ef999f9e94e8d14eb018c17c187dffbe009e02.html
- CRS, Navy carrier strike group primer (2024): https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2024-12-12_IF10486_5a77a12cd1383d8a880d17c8afced3df1ee48378.html
- Soviet submarine B-59 (1962): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_submarine_B-59
Blast and burn figures: the channel's scenario engine, from Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the group, the submarine, the burst point and the 10-kiloton yield are ours, a scenario, not a forecast.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble; thumbnail backgrounds generated with Google Gemini. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
